books.title: The Open Road
books.subtitle: English for your next adventure
books.description: Explore the language of travel through original dialogues, practical phrases, and listening activities.

resources.title: A new beginning
resources.transcript: Hello! Welcome to your English class. My name is Alex. I am curious about the world, and I love learning new things. Today, we will start a new journey together. Listen carefully, ask questions, and be kind to your classmates. A little practice every day makes a big difference. Let us begin.

lessons.title: Your next stop
lessons.description: Useful phrases for finding your way in a new city.

sections.title: Ask for directions
sections.body: Begin politely. 'Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the station?' Useful direction words include straight ahead, turn left, turn right, next to, and opposite.

sections.title: Check you understood
sections.body: Repeat the key information. 'So I turn left at the cafe?' If you need help, say 'Could you repeat that, please?' Thank the person before you leave.

lessons.question: What does 'opposite the library' mean?
lessons.explanation: Opposite means on the other side, facing something.

lessons.title: Yesterday in a few words
lessons.description: Describe a finished day using the past simple.

sections.title: Talk about a finished action
sections.body: Use the past simple for an action completed at a known past time. 'We visited our neighbour yesterday.' Regular verbs usually add -ed. Irregular verbs change. Go becomes went. 'I went to the festival on Saturday.'

sections.title: Ask about yesterday
sections.body: Use did and the base verb. 'Did you enjoy the festival?' For a negative, use did not. 'We did not stay late.' Tell a partner about yesterday using three finished actions.

lessons.question: Choose the correct past-simple question.
lessons.explanation: After did, use the base verb visit rather than visited.

lessons.title: Plans for the weekend
lessons.description: Talk about intentions with going to.

sections.title: Say what you intend to do
sections.body: Use am, is, or are with going to and the base verb. 'I am going to invite a friend.' 'We are going to prepare lunch.' These are plans you have already thought about.

sections.title: Ask and respond
sections.body: Ask 'What are you going to do tomorrow?' Add a time or a place to your answer. 'I am going to repair my bicycle in the garden.' Share one plan with a partner and ask a follow-up question.

lessons.question: Which sentence describes a future intention?
options: We are going to prepare lunch tomorrow.
lessons.explanation: Going to describes the intention, and tomorrow makes the future time clear.
